fields.history: ===Origin=== thumb|right|Ororo with her parents Ororo Munroe is the descendant of an ancient line of African priestesses, all of whom had white hair, blue eyes, and the potential to wield magic. For many generations her maternal ancestors lived in the hidden village in Kenya and served as its leaders, passing the power from mother to daughter. Her mother, N'Daré, was the tribe's princess and meant to become their next leader, but she rebelled against this tradition and escaped from the village. Instead she went to study in the university, where she met an American student David Munroe. The two fell in love and married. N'Daré followed David to the United States of America, they settled in the Harlem and gave birth to Ororo. Accustomed to being treated as a princess, N'Daré felt uncomfortable in America where she was treated badly for her skin color, and convinced David that they shouldn't endure it, and definitely shouldn't let their daughter grow up in such an environment. When Ororo was 6 months old David got an offer for a job in Egypt and the family moved to Cairo. thumb|right|Parents' death The family lived happily there. N'Daré told her young daughter stories about their lineage of queens and priestesses, and about her grandmother, who had the same white hair and blue eyes and possessed legendary magical skills. N'Daré also showed young Ororo the ancient ruby that was passed in their family from mother to daughter for countless generations. David in turn told her stories about Harlem where they both were born and where they lived before moving to Cairo. When Ororo was 6 years old, a plane crash destroyed their home. Ororo's parents were killed, but she survived, buried under rubble near their dead bodies. This traumatizing effect left Ororo with the severe claustrophobia that still afflicts her today. Ororo managed to escape the rubble of her shattered home with nothing but the tattered clothes on her back and her mother's ancestral ruby. ===Street Thief=== right|thumb|Stealing from Charles Xavier (Earth-616)|Charles Xavier Homeless and orphaned, Ororo was found by a gang of street urchins who took her to their master, Achmed El Gibár. Achmed trained Ororo how to survive on the streets, begging, stealing and picking both pockets and locks. At 6 years old, one of her first targets was an American tourist. She stole his wallet, but the man proved no easy mark, as he was Charles Xavier, a powerful mutant telepath who used his abilities to stop the theft. At that moment, Xavier was psionically attacked by another mutant, Amahl Farouk (absolute ruler of Cairo's thieves), and Ororo used the opportunity to escape. Xavier, who acknowledged she was a mutant from her brainwaves, declined to contact Ororo at this point, not wanting to shock the young girl with the true nature of her powers. thumb|left|Stealing the Heart of Eternal Darkness Achmed El Gibár extensively trained Ororo and within a year she became his prize pupil, the best thief in Cairo. She stole to live and lived to steal. Itching to prove her skills, Ororo looked for harder targets and new challenges. When she learned about a treasure guarded in a mansion outside of Cairo, young thief infiltrated it and stole the Heart of Eternal Darkness. Unexpectedly once she took away the ruby, entire mansion exploded and killed everyone inside. Ororo managed to escape and proudly returned to her teacher to show-off, but was instead scolded. He took the ruby from her for safekeeping. Unknowingly to both of them, the mansion belonged to an immortal mutant Candra, and the Heart contained her life force and power. Ororo grew to hate her parents for abandoning her, and even refused to use her real name for several years, preferring to use name "Snow-top" that was given to her by other urchins. When she was 8 years old, she was sent on her first solo mission to steal a box from the museum. She successfully completed the mission and proudly returned to Achmed El Gibár. Inside the box was the photo of Ororo and her parents, and Achmed told her that great thief hides from others, not herself and she should accept her true name. She refused initially, but eventually thanked Achmed, mourned her parents and accepted her name. thumb|right|With Achmed's urchins At around 10 years old Ororo became experienced enough for Achmed El Gibár to trust her to lead two other thieves, Hakiim and Nari as a small team. During one of their missions to steal food for all the urchins, Hakiim was almost caught by the guards. Nari believed that it was more important to deliver the food, so she escaped. Ororo stayed behind to save Hakiim, but she couldn't do much to the guards. The kids were saved by their teacher and returned with him to their home, where Nari was bragging how good of a thief she was. fields.notes: Storm is best friends with Jean Grey. Storm was one of the first mutants that Professor Xavier met before founding the X-Men. Storm's white hair apparently is part of her family legacy, being unrelated to her mutation, as states that "born with white hair and blue eyes, [her] genetic mutation would not manifest until she reached adolescence." Chris Claremont, the writer of , hinted that Storm was bisexual. However, due to Jim Shooter's anti-gay policies, her relationship with Yukio remained entirely subtextual. In , an AXIS inversion spell caused Storm to kiss a woman on panel. Writer Frank Tieri tweeted that this kiss exemplified Ororo's bisexuality, citing her relationship with Yukio as another example. Al Ewing, the writer of and , also wrote Ororo as bisexual during his tenure on the character.
fields.trivia: Storm was originally conceived by Dave Cockrum as "the Black Cat," a character who could transform into a feline creature or a house cat. The character was shelved for a time, along with the rest of the new X-Men project, and ultimately made redundant by the large number of cat-themed characters that had been introduced in the interim. When the project resumed, it was decided that the team needed another female character, and Roy Thomas suggested replacing the weather-controlling Typhoon with a female equivalent. Cockrum then quickly outlined the idea for Storm, leaving the Black Cat costume unchanged but changing the character's hair from brunette to white. In the 70s, Dave Cockrum planned to create an all-female team named The Furies which teamed-up Storm with Clea, Tigra, Namorita, Dragonfly, and a new character called Moon Fang. Despite the book being tentatively greenlit, Cockrum never finished the plot for the team's first story, and the idea eventually fell apart. The name "Ororo" means "Beauty". When T'Challa first heard her name, he immediately recognized it as Kenyan, even though there is no Kenyan language; Kenya has two official languages, Swahili and English, and almost are used across the country. When she married King T'Challa and became a queen of Wakanda, her married name was Ororo Iqadi T'Challa, while the short form of her royal title was Ororo Komo Wakandas. The full form of her title was never stated, but, according to Ororo, in Hausa dialect it took around five minutes to recite it. In while Storm was in the hospital after being reverted into a pre-teen body, one of the doctors said, "But her features don't fit any conventional classification. Not Negroid, Caucasian, or Oriental -- Yet somehow, an amalgam of the rarest elements of them all." Storm is currently one of the only people on Earth-616 who has been a member of the X-Men, Avengers, and Fantastic Four. The others are Spider-Man and Wolverine. Storm's original spacious attic garden and bed room was made for her by Nightcrawler. With the destruction of the original X-Mansion, Storm, has since taken up residency and rebuilt her garden in one of the many free floating towers of the new Grey School. Ororo was a partial nudist, due to her time being worshipped as a goddess, and during her time with X-Men. She eventually learned from Jean to dress regularly in clothing. In celebration of Marvel Comics 80th anniversary, Storm, along with Mystique and Dark Phoenix were featured in a special line of fashion dolls. In , Ororo's birth year is given as being late 1950 or early 1951, thus making her 25 during the issue at hand. However, this should be considered non-canonical per the Sliding Timescale of Earth-616. Ororo's age at the time she joined the X-Men is unclear. She left Cairo when she was around 12 and travelled for almost a year, but was still 12 when she first met T'Challa. They travelled together for some time before she settled in Uzuri, so presumably she was around 13 at the time. It wasn't specified for how long she stayed with the tribe, but it was mentioned that there were "years of drought" she helped to deal with. When she visited her father's old apartment in Harlem, Ororo mentioned that it was "over twenty years ago" since she lived there with her parents. On another occasion she mentioned what she first encountered Charles Xavier when she was 6 years old and hadn't met him again "for almost two decades". Another occasion shows that Ororo is 30 years old . So, presumably she was at least 20/21 years old when she joined the X-Men. Ororo had on several occasions invoked and prayed to a unknown goddess she referred to as just "Goddess", the "Bright Lady" and "Mother Nature"/"Mother Earth", confirmed to be Elder Goddesses Oshtur and Gaia. In case of Oshtur, it is possible that she was worshipped by her family for generations, since her ancestor Ashake was Oshtur's disciple and priestess. Another possibility is what Ororo started to worship the Bright Lady under the influence of her teacher Achmed El Gibár, who prayed to the Bright Lady as well. She prayed to the Bright Lady since her childhood. Storm also claimed that her powers were bestowed to her by the earth mother Gaia. The Rain Queens from from people (South Africa) are called Mujaji or Modjadji, who possibly inspired the creation of the goddess Mujaji, one of the Orisha, the Gods of Wakanda. The writer of , Angélique Roché, confirmed Storm was chosen to be archived for all of eternity due to being the linchpin of a timeline. The writer stated major events around Storm molds and shifts the timeline, and Storm's character strongly impacts the timeline. ===Awards=== For the Glyph Comics Awards in 2007, Ororo was the most successful comic and was the winner for the best comic of the year, by Eric Jerome Dickey, David Yardin & Lan Medina and Jay Leisten & Sean Parsons. ororo munroe moira vii 1.origin: ===Sins of Sinister: First Decade=== Storm's origins and past equal those of her mainstream counterpart, in which she was an important political figure in the Quiet Council of Krakoa and the Great Ring of Arakko. The timeline diverged due to Mister Sinister's machinations of tainting humanity and mutandom by introducing his vile genome to uncountable victims through the Resurrection Protocols. By rejecting resurrection, Storm was free from his influence, but was also unaware that her closest allies had been corrupted versions of Sinister. One year later, the Quiet Council secretly lobotomized the consciousness of Krakoa and blamed Orchis for the attack, prompting Storm join the Avengers and the X-Men in striking at Orchis' forces together. Storm participated in the killing of Nimrod alongside with Thor. Over the following years, mutantkind machinated their control over the planet, eliminating opposition through treachery and deception. Their cruel ascension turned Storm disillusioned with her mission. Five years after Sinister had secretly infiltrated mutant society, Storm noticed that Nightcrawler had been replaced by an impostor, prompting Mister Sinister to reveal himself and his actions. The Quiet Council attempted to subdue Storm, but she escaped to Peru thanks to Lactuca, where she was met by Destiny and Mystique who proposed an alliance. left|150px Storm resisted in Arakko for the following years, leading her Brotherhood of Mutants against Mister Sinister's cloned Chimeras. However, a clone of Legion was used to obliterate Planet Arakko, and the few Arakkii survivors retread into hiding. Having lost much, Storm remained in the debris of Arakko, dubbed Asteroid S, with her right-hand man Jon Ironfire, former S.W.O.R.D. agents Cable and Wiz Kid and the Arakkii Khora of the Burning Heart and Quick as part of her Brotherhood. Mystique eventually approached Storm in Asteroid S to reveal about Mister Sinister's Moira Engine, a machine that could reset reality via clones of Moira. Storm and the Brotherhood went to Muir Island to retrieve Mister Sinister's lab, but Mystique betrayed them by impersonating Wiz Kid. She mortally wounded Storm, paralyzing her, and took the engine with her to the World Farm under Orbis Stellaris' guidance. ===Year 100=== Over the course of a century, Storm led the underground freedom fighters known as the Brotherhood to fight against both Sinister's Red Diamond Empire and Stellaris' Interstellar Compact. Storm became known as "the Old Witch." A rival insurgent cell called the Freedom Force trasmitted the location and schematics of the Compact's Death Sphere to Arakko Base. After Mystique's death, Destiny joined with Storm and the Brotherhood to set off the Moira Engine and reset the timeline. They attacked the Death Sphere, but before they destroyed the Center-Sun that contained the Moiras, Storm had Destiny killed. Storm believed that Arrako's destruction did not justify eliminating an entire timeline so her true plan was to teleport the Moiras away to defuse and guard. Khora magnified Storm's mutant powers and she mixed it with magic to open a wormhole that teleported the World Farm away. However, the price of this feat was her life and she died smiling. ===Year 1000=== Over the next 900 years, Storm's brotherhood, now led by Jon Ironfire, turned the World Farm into an impregnable fortress. After 900 years of searching, Mr. Sinister finally found the World Farm and his lab. Pursued by an Empire of the Red Diamond armada, Sinister and Ironfire entered into a temporary alliance. Sinister used genetic material of Storm and Hope Summers, together with five Brotherhood mutants, to resurrect Storm, though without the memories of the original. Boosted by Khora, Storm destroyed the armada. Lacking the experience of her original self, Storm did not shield herself from the resultant radiation, and died once again.

orphan.name: Orphan
orphan.origin: Orphan was some form of sentient alien technology, which several millennia prior to the modern age inhabited an alien mothership which crashed in Australia. Its crew on board all perished and was eventually discovered by an Aboriginal tribe. For generations they looked after and protected it, anointing one of their own as the "Dreamguard" to Orphan and Orphan used his ability to bring the dreams of the tribe to life. In the modern age, two bank robbers Shane Mundy and Alf Robbins discovered the dreamland and killed its current dreamguard. Robbins and Mundy went to sleep inside Orphan, who merged with Mundy but did not realize that Mundy was a morally corrupt person began to unleashed monsters on the neighboring town. This attack attracted Force Works who eventually tracked Orphan down and Mundy used Orphan to lock each member in their own personal nightmare, while revealing his origins to Willie Walkaway. After a short battle with Mundy's monsters they were able to free Orphan and Willie stayed to become Orphan's new dreamguard.

orphan maker anya.name: Orphan Maker (Anya)
orphan maker anya.origin: Orphan Maker was a former Red Room assassin who hadn't killed anyone in years. When a new incarnation of the Red Room emerged and started murdering all competition, from Hydra to even former Red Room agents, Orphan Maker attacked Hawkeye and Winter Soldier while they were staking out a Red Room safe house in Manhattan, believing the Winter Soldier to be behind the murders. Hawkeye defused the situation, but before Orphan Maker could reveal who was behind the Red Room emergence, she was abruptly shot in the head by the returned Black Widow, who was also opposing the Red Room. When she was destroying the cloning program responsible for bringing her back to life, Black Widow had the psychic Epsilon Red transfer Anya's memories to a brain-dead clone body to bring her back to life.

orphelus.name: Orphelus
orphelus.origin: Orphelus was a Roman magician born in Italy. During the third century, he was a legionary, and found a magical pool of blood in Britain. Drinking the blood gave him a greatly extended life, but after seventeen hundred years, he came to see his immortality as a sin. In the modern era, Orphelus lured Dracula to the pool, believing both of them needed to die. He used a magical amulet to destroy the blood pool and died as it boiled away. Dracula was also badly injured, but his vampiric powers allowed him to survive.

orpheus.name: Orpheus
orpheus.origin: ===Origin=== Orpheus was an Ancient Greek hero endowed with superhuman musical skills. He was the son of King Oeagrus and Calliope of Thrace. Apollo gave Orpheus his first lyre. Orpheus's singing and playing were so beautiful that animals and even trees and rocks moved about him in dance. ===Quest for the Golden Fleece=== Orpheus joined the expedition of the Argonauts on hunting the Golden Fleece. ===Journey to the Underworld=== He later married Eurydice, but she was killed by a snakebite. Overcome with grief, Orpheus traveled to Hades, the Underworld itself to attempt to bring Eurydice back to life. With his singing and playing he charmed the ferryman Charon and the three headed dog Cerberus, guardians of the River Styx. His music and grief so moved Hades allowed to take Eurydice with him back to the world of life and light. Hades set one condition, however: upon leaving the land of death, both Orpheus and Eurydice were forbidden to look back. The couple climbed up toward the opening into the land of the living, and Orpheus, seeing the Sun again, turned back to share his delight with Eurydice in that moment, she disappeared.

orrek.name: Orrek
orrek.origin: In 6,000 BC, which was about 12,000 years after Atlantis sank beneath the ocean, Prince Orrek of the nomadic Homo mermani Eastern Sea tribe arrived at the ruins of Atlantis. He travelled with his brother King Stegor who led the army to battle the army of the Western Sea led by King Tanas. The warring nations both bid to conquer the city and its hidden treasures. King Stegor died in the battle by the Queen Elanna of the Western Sea. Orrek, then sent Prince Kamuu on patrol, with the plan that the prince would be killed, so he could attain the throne of the tribe.

orrgo.name: Orrgo
orrgo.origin: ===Invasion Attempts=== Ten thousand years ago Orrgo attempted to conquer the Earth, but was eventually thwarted by Ulysses Bloodstone using a spear that was empowered by the Star of Capistan and an idol statue called the God From Beyond. This forced the alien invader to retreat for millennia. In May of 1961, two billion miles from Earth, the imperialistic race called the Mentelleronites discussed their plan to conquer the planet Earth. Immediately, one of the Mentelleronites volunteered to be the planet's invader was none other than Orrgo. He believed his race to be so superior to the humans that he could accomplish the feat single-handedly. Teleporting himself across the galaxy, Orrgo materialized in a circus in an American town and told the people present to bow to him as he had come to conquer the Earth. The police and military were called out to oppose Orrgo, but no one proved capable of withstanding his awesome power. thumb|left|300px|The effects of Orrgo's power After hypnotizing all of the world's population, Orrgo decided to sleep near the circus where he had originally materialized. Jo-Jo the circus gorilla became infuriated that his hypnotized master had not moved to feed him. Breaking out of his cage, Jo-Jo found a sleeping Orrgo and sensed that he was responsible for his hunger. The mighty ape then struck down Orrgo, supposedly killing him and saving the world. The others on Orrgo's world sensed that their brother had been defeated and thus decided not to try to invade Earth again, as they must be more powerful than originally thought. Later Orrgo was revived as a pawn by the Headmen, M.O.D.O.K., and AIM. They had acquired the God From Beyond statue, the same ancient artifact which Ulysses used to control Orrgo to remove him from Earth. They used him in their schemes of world domination, coming into conflict with the Defenders. He was eventually freed when the Defenders got the idol from the Headmen and smashed it. Before Orrgo could attempt to attack anyone of his own will, Hellcat humiliated him by pointing out his failures, shaming the invader to retreat into space. ===Agent of S.H.I.E.L.D.=== Some time later, Orrgo snuck back to Earth as one of the refugees outside of Monster Metropolis after Monster Island was attacked by the Hunter of Monster Special Forces. At some point, it appears that Orrgo was captured by S.H.I.E.L.D., as he was among the Howling Commandos who launched an attack on Merlin's forces. Orrgo, along with Goom and a Double-Headed Krackalakassian, were briefly captured by Amadeus and Maddy Cho. Orrgo later joined another incarnation of the Howling Commandos led by Dum-Dum Dugan. Due to Orrgo's enormous size, he is not a field member of the team but was used as technical support and communications. He enjoys chaotic events. Despite the very nature of many of his teammates, Orrgo did not believe in the supernatural. While investigating the secret projects of Area 13, Orrgo was discovered by Paul Kraye and sent to Pleasant Hill to be turned into a dog. During his time with the team he was forced to face his trauma of when Jo-Jo violently killed him in his sleep, eventually overcoming it with help from his teammates. ===Monsters Unleashed=== During the Leviathon Tide's attack on Earth, Orrgo was one of the numerous monsters independent of the Tide summoned by young Inhuman Kei Kawade to help fend off the invading forces. During the siege, he aided Earth's heroes at San Diego alongside Fin Fang Foom, Goom, and Googam. Once the Leviathons were defeated, Orrgo continued to work for S.T.A.K.E.. During the events of Hydra's regime over the America, S.T.A.K.E. was used to hunt down fugitives. During one encounter Orrgo fought against Devil Dinosaur and quickly lost. Orrgo was later seen training Kid Juggernaut at Avengers Academy.

orrible oress.name: Orrible Oress
orrible oress.origin: Orrible Oress was a mobster who operated out of the town of Middleton in the 1940's. Developing a special kind of exploding light bulb, Oress had his men plant them all over the city, leaving city officials stumped where the the explosive bulbs could be placed. This forced the mayor to order a mandatory blackout of the city. This played into Oress' plan as he sent send his minions out to commit a large scale robbery. This was witnessed by police officer Pat Murphy who donned his guise of the homeless super-hero known as the Vagabond. The hero followed Orrible's gang back to his windmill hide out. There, the hero defeated Oress' gang, and in a one-on-one battle, the Vagabond proved the superior opponent, even though Orrible was armed with a gun and a knife. In the end, Oress was thrown from the top of the windmill to his death. His gang was apprehended shortly thereafter.

orson kasloff.name: Orson Kasloff
orson kasloff.origin: Professor Orson Kasloff was a brilliant scientist chemist, considered by some the foremost analytical chemist in the world, who felt that he didn't earn enough money for his scientific work and turned to crime. When his first attempt at a break-in failed because he hadn't considered burglar alarms, he decided to search out other criminals to partner up with. Failing to make contact with the underworld, he saw the Human Torch in action and decided to defeat the young hero in order to impress the underworld. He bought an old castle and built an armored suit made out of asbestos. He was defeated and turned over to the police by the Human Torch. Lacking villainous plans, he hoped to avenge himself from the Torch, but Storm died before he could. Kasloff tried to start back his criminal career, as he was annoyed that people would forget him with Johnny Storm dead. He tried to rob a fast food restaurant, now carrying around an air canister due to having survived cancer, probably due to the suit itself, but was annoyed to find the cashier was afraid of him because he was wearing asbestos and feared for her health. Asbestos Man ran into the Great Lakes Avengers who were on the run from a fear influenced mob themselves. They all assumed fighting stances surrounding Orson, but since Orson wasn't willing to fight and no one in the team was willing to even touch a man wearing an asbestos suit they all ended up staying that way for hours until they all gave up. Orson confided in them his fears of no one remembering him and being an awful super villain. Mr. Immortal was able to get him to surrender quietly with the promise that they would remember him as one of their villains (though they refused his toxic mask as a trophy). He was then removed by an ambulance and hazmat-suited staff. He was later stated by Johnny Storm to have died, presumably from his condition. However he, or someone wearing his costume, was in prison with Ziggy Pig and Silly Seal.

orson randall.name: Orson Randall
orson randall.species: Human who defeated Shou-Lao the Undying
orson randall.origin: ===Early Life=== Orson Randall was born in the mystical city of K'un-Lun after his father's airship crashed into the mystical city during one of its periodic materializations on the Earthly plane. He was adopted as a member of the city; trained by the Thunderer, educated by Yu-Ti, and eventually defeated Shou-Lao when he was seventeen to become the city's champion, the Immortal Iron Fist. At some point, he faced and overcame the Challenge of the Many. Orson went on to face the Challenge of The One and bested him, earning his position as the Iron Fist. However, Yu-Ti had programmed The One to lose against Orson, thus guaranteeing Orson's position as the Iron Fist. When Orson matured, he left the city, as many Iron Fists before him had. ===World War I=== During WWI, he joined a group of heroes who fought together as the Freedom's Five. The team consisted of Phantom Eagle, Union Jack, Crimson Cavalier (Jean-Luc Batroc), and a new Sir Steel (Ned Chapel). Together the heroes battled the Martians. The fighting in WWI affected Randall deeply. After the war ended he stayed in France, and sometime before 1926 he began his addiction to drugs as a way to escape from the memories. ===Tournament of the Heavenly Cities=== In 1933, he was recalled for the Tournament of Heavenly Cities. Upon his return, however, he refused to fight in the tournament, having been changed by seeing too much blood and violence in his time out of the city. When confronted by his would-be opponents, attempting to strip him of his station, he lashed out, killing the champion of K'un-Zi. With no other options left to him he took the Book of the Iron Fist, containing the knowledge and kung-fu of the Iron Fists that came before and readable only by Iron Fists, and fled the city to New York. thumb|left|Orson Randall dressed in his Iron Fist suit Lei-Kung was dispatched to find Randall, but taking pity on him, reported back that he was deceased. Believed to be dead, Randall spent the next few years of his life--alongside his "biographer" Ernst Erskine--having adventures. ===Confederates of the Curious=== Orson created the Confederates of the Curious to function as a prototype for later superheroic teams such as the Invaders and Avengers. The first by Randall’s side was Lucky Pierre (Ernst Erskine), or L.P. as Orson referred to him often. L.P. was there when Orson faced the Lightning Lords of Nepal and their mistress, the Bride of Nine Spiders. After what could have been their last venture together, Orson and L.P. began to recruit others, misfits just as the two of them, and suddenly, their adventures turned into missions. Each member of the team had their roles to play, and all were at the peak of their game. The Contessa played an integral part in a later task to retrieve Orson’s Last Will and Testament from the Nine-Fold Daughters of Xao. Then as Randall was hunted by the Prince of Orphans, it was Shadu the Shady that was the first to be alerted to the Prince’s presence, and it was Chores MacGillicuddy that put his life on the line to save Randall from that very same menace after escaping imprisonment by the Cowgirls from Hell. It was after that battle that Orson dissolved the group because he did not want his friends to pay for his crimes. Eventually Randall and the Prince of Orphans were able to get past their differences, around the time of WWII when the Prince learned his people had been lying to him. ===Avoiding the Ch'i-Lin=== The Iron Fist Slayer Zhou Cheng attacked Randall on his 33rd birthday in 1934, tracking him by sensing the chi of Shou-Lao within him. Zhou intended to kill Randall for the Ch'i-Lin so it could use his heart to access the egg of Shou-Lao the Undying, which it sought to consume. Randall fought off Zhou and decided to mask the "scent" of his chi by drowning himself in hardline drugs. ===Wendell Rand=== Still going on adventures, Randall met and adopted as a ward a young Wendell Rand and began both training him to fight and filling his head with stories of the mystical K'un-Lun and the Iron Fist. Randall's growing opium addiction did nothing to stem his vast fortune or his adventures, and sometime after the 1960s he was believed to have "died" and the majority of his fortune was willed to Wendell Rand, while also being shared with his former comrades to ensure they would want for nothing. However, Randall was not actually dead, just lost in his addictions in Thailand. ===Danny Rand=== As the next Tournament of Heavenly Cities neared Davos, the Steel Serpent sought him out to kill him, which only caused him to fly to New York. In New York, when he used his Iron Fist powers during a battle, Danny Rand felt great pain. Rand attempted to track him down, but failed, only to find him back in his office. The older Iron Fist filled in the younger on their histories between battles with Hydra and Davos, during the latter Randall sacrificed himself to transfer his power to Rand. ===Damnation=== Mephisto offered Randall a chance to r

orson whales.name: Orson Whales
orson whales.first_appearance: Peter Porker, The Spectacular Spider-Ham Vol 1 9
orson whales.origin: Orson Whales was an anthropomorphic whale who had succeeded as a radio star, staging a mock invasion of aliens from Mars, and later as a film director. Whales' friend J. Jonah Jackal believed that Whales had been the best film director, but Hollywood sharks (who were likely literal sharks) kicked him away from their city. As an elderly whale, Whales lived in a suburban environment in rural New Jersey, taking meager pleasure in eating (not meagerly eating, mind you). Whales was still famous to some extent, partly due to his immense physical size - a Japanese joke suggested that Whales and giant monster Hog-zilla could almost share shirt size (although Hog-zilla did not wear a shirt). Whales then had a "close encounter of the third kind" when an alien from outer space (later called B.O.) knocked at his door. Because of his previous martial invasion radio show, Whales was unable to convince his neighbors of the existence of this alien. Whales then decided to sent the alien, by post, to his friend Jackal with a note so that Jackal, by then a reputed newspaper editor, could inform the world about the real nature of the alien. However, Jackal was unable to grab hold of the alien, who returned to outer space; Jackal decided not to report about B.O. without proof.

ort beast.name: Ort-Beast
ort beast.origin: The Ort-Beast is an extradimensional alien. It inhabits a pocket universe which is either within the Shadow Cloak of Devil-Slayer, or accessed through the Cloak. Its world is ever-changing, but the creature considers it the best of all possible worlds. It is unclear whether the Ort-Beast has experiences with other worlds. The Ort-Beast has been described by Devil-Slayer as one of the crystalline inhabitants of its world. Whether there are actually others like it is unconfirmed. None has been depicted. The creature has been described as both sentient and highly intelligent, but apparently can not properly speak. Its only vocalization is repeating the word "Ort", from which its name derives. It has red skin, claws in its hands, and a beak in its face. At some point, the Ort-Beast encountered and fought the Hulk, who was briefly trapped in its world. The Hulk believed that the creature was trying to eat him, but its motivation is somewhat unclear. The Ort-Beast viewed him as a "soft green being", and the narration describes the Hulk as the creature's odd playmate. Due to the realm around them which is constantly changing, the two combatants could not get the upper hand in this combat. The Ort-Beast's claws were prevented from harming the Hulk, while the Beast teleported away from his fists when he attacked. The Hulk was unhappy with this ever-changing world which prevented him from smashing monsters. He threatened to smash the world itself. The Ort-Beast reappeared behind the Hulk's back, but it was quite puzzled by his words. It wondered why the Hulk was dissatisfied with the world. Devil-Slayer and Valkyrie interrupted the fight, by offering the Hulk a chance to return to Earth. The Hulk attacked Devil-Slayer, who was the one who trapped him in the first place. The Ort-Beast briefly attempted to follow the Hulk. When the Hulk disappeared (teleported away by Devil-Slayer), the creature was left alone in its world again. At a later point, Hellcat was practicing with her own version of the Shadow Cloak, and was also trying to entertain the Hulk. She tried pulling something out of the teleportation cloak, and accidentally pulled out the head of the Ort-Beast. Hulk went into attack mode and assaulted the Shadow Cloak, accidentally hurting Hellcat in the process. During the attack, the Ort-Beast disappeared. Probably having returned to its own world.

She tried pulling something out of the teleportation cloak, and accidentally pulled out the head of the Ort-Beast. Hulk went into attack mode and assaulted the Shadow Cloak, accidentally hurting Hellcat in the process. During the attack, the Ort-Beast disappeared. Probably having returned to its own world.

weaknesses: The creature cannot speak any coherent language, and just keeps repeating "Ort". This limits its ability to communicate with others.

ortlinda.name: Ortlinda
ortlinda.origin: When Hela had taken over Valhalla and turned it into a reflection of her own realm, Niffleheim, Odin sent Ortlinda and the rest of the Valkyrior ahead of him to fight off Hela, but she and her sisters were slain by Hela's minions. When Odin got there, he plead with Hela to bring them back to life and stop her madness, but she explained that after a recent encounter with Thor and Lady Sif, she realized that she had wanted to express her own feelings of compassion and desire to be a woman, but could not since she was burdened with being the goddess of death. Odin then took pity on Hela and granted her the wisdom and knowledge she sought. She went back to Niffleheilm, allowing Valhalla to return to its original form, resurrecting Ortlinda and the rest of the Valkyries in the process.

orvarg.name: Orvarg
orvarg.origin: Orvarg was a Storm Giant warrior, seemingly a leader subordinated to Grim Graybeard. Along with five other Storm Giants, he was tasked to follow Grid, Vidar Odinson's mother, as Grim Graybeard had rallied the Storm Giants' armies to join Bjorn the White's Frost Giants and their champion Ymir. Thor, on his way to find his half-brother (as Hoder had prophetized Vidar's role in the coming conflict) detected them, and stealthily spied upon them, learning their goals and that Ymir had joined them, tanks to a Storm Giant Orvarg beat up as he kept speaking those vital information out loud. Thor then attacked them, and with the timely arrival of Vidar, Orvarg's crew was defeated, but he escaped, capturing Grid in the process, taking her hostage and threatening to kill her if Vidar didn't surrendered to him. He then delivered her to the Giants leaders Grim Graybeard and Bjorn the White, who intended respectively intended to use her as a gift to Odin or as a bait for Vidar.

orville jones.name: Orville Jones
orville jones.origin: Orville Jones showed up on Kid Colt's 17th birthday, challenging the Kid to a shootout. The Kid accepted the challenge but as the fight was set to begin some of the townsfolk realized that Orville Jones was the notorious hypnotist that hypnotized his opponents into losing during shootouts. No one was able to reveal the truth to Kid Colt as the shootout had already begun. Everyone was surprised when the Kid shot the guns from Orville’s hands. Kid Colt then told everyone that his father had taught him to look at a man’s hands instead of his face, explaining why he was unaffected by Jones' powers of hypnotism.

orwell taylor.name: Orwell Taylor
orwell taylor.origin: Orwell Taylor was once a General in the United States Army. Orwell and his wife had two sons, Maxwell and Hugh Taylor. As an adult, Hugh joined the Army where he became friends with Samuel Caulkin and after he left the Army he got a job working at the superhuman prison known as the Vault where he became close friends with Curtis Elkins. Hugh was smothered to death by Venom. Orwell, mad with grief, wanted to find a way to avenge the death of his son. Orwell gathered together several of his son Hugh's former army buddies and fellow guardsmen at the vault and outfitted them with armor based on the armor the Guardsman wore (which was based on designs stolen from Iron Man. Maxwell become "Screech", Samuel Caulkin become "Ramshot", and Curtis Elkins become "Sentry". He named this group the Jury and made it their mission to bring Venom to justice. Orwell and the Jury failed in their first outing against Venom. Later they kidnapped and drugged Spider-Man and tricked him into helping them steal a government transporter ray that they planned to modify to kill Venom. Again they met with failure. Orwell and the Jury later began to get away from their original goals and began working with the Life Foundation. Orwell was eventually apprehended by the authorities for his illegal dealings with the Life Foundation.

osamu moroboshi.name: Osamu Moroboshi
osamu moroboshi.origin: Osamu Moroboshi was the CEO of Moroboshi International, a competitor of Stark International. At some unspecified point in time, he came into contact with Controller, who implanted him with a more advanced, undetectable version of his slave discs. Still recovering from the grievous injuries he suffered during the Armor Wars, Controller used Moroboshi as a proxy in an elaborate plan to take control of Stark International and use its resources to heal his broken body. Moroboshi contacted Justin Hammer and several representatives from HYDRA, the Hand, and Roxxon Energy representing a mysterious "patron." After Tony Stark was believed to have died from neurocellular degradation, Moroboshi enacted a plan to place Morgan Stark as the figurehead CEO, under the reasoning that Morgan was Tony's next of kin. This plan was complicated by the fact that Tony had willed the company to James Rhodes, so Morgan attempted to remove Rhodes by planting evidence that framed Rhodes for Tony's murder. This plan quickly fell apart when Tony was revealed to be alive, and Moroboshi began to saw Morgan as a liability that could implicate him. Moroboshi attempted to cover his tracks by deploying battle droids to assassinate Rhodes, but this plot failed when Rhodes, in his War Machine armor, and Iron Man's Telepresence Armor defeated the robot stormtroopers in a standing battle. With Morgan implicated in the conspiracy and attempting to flee the country, Moroboshi has Berserker-7 shoot the tires out of his car, sending him careening off a cliff. Moroboshi calls his patron, telling him there is now nothing that can be traced back to them. But Moroboshi's own usefulness had also come to an end. Controller activated a kill switch in Moroboshi's slave disc, killing him and making it look like he died of a stroke.

Still recovering from the grievous injuries he suffered during the Armor Wars, Controller used Moroboshi as a proxy in an elaborate plan to take control of Stark International and use its resources to heal his broken body. Moroboshi contacted Justin Hammer and several representatives from HYDRA, the Hand, and Roxxon Energy representing a mysterious "patron." After Tony Stark was believed to have died from neurocellular degradation, Moroboshi enacted a plan to place Morgan Stark as the figurehead CEO, under the reasoning that Morgan was Tony's next of kin. This plan was complicated by the fact that Tony had willed the company to James Rhodes, so Morgan attempted to remove Rhodes by planting evidence that framed Rhodes for Tony's murder. This plan quickly fell apart when Tony was revealed to be alive, and Moroboshi began to saw Morgan as a liability that could implicate him. Moroboshi attempted to cover his tracks by deploying battle droids to assassinate Rhodes, but this plot failed when Rhodes, in his War Machine armor, and Iron Man's Telepresence Armor defeated the robot stormtroopers in a standing battle. With Morgan implicated in the conspiracy and attempting to flee the country, Moroboshi has Berserker-7 shoot the tires out of his car, sending him careening off a cliff. Moroboshi calls his patron, telling him there is now nothing that can be traced back to them. But Moroboshi's own usefulness had also come to an end. Controller activated a kill switch in Moroboshi's slave disc, killing him and making it look like he died of a stroke.

oscar stamp.first_appearance: Further Adventures of Cyclops and Phoenix Vol 1 2
oscar stamp.origin: In the year 1859, Oscar Stamp was part of a group of Marauders, who kidnapped freaks, fools, and all types of misshapen folk off the streets of London and took them underground. Dr. Nathaniel Essex hired the thugs to continue their work, so he could perform experiments on the victims in the name of science. One of them was a boy, named Danny Edge, who had stopped talking after witnessing the murder of his parents. After awakening, the immortal mutant, En Sabah Nur, Nur ordered the Marauders to take him to Dr. Essex; meanwhile, the time-travelers, Cyclops and Phoenix, arrived. Cyclops and Phoenix thwarted Nur and Mister Sinister's plan to conquer the United Kingdom and Oscar and Daniel journeyed to America to start a new life. At the immigration office, they claimed to be father and son, by the name of Summers, inspired by the married couple that had saved them from their fates.

oshemar.name: Oshemar
oshemar.origin: An inventor from an alien dimension known as the Caldaran Dominions, Oshemar's people fought a long war against the Sextus Hive, losing much in the war. As the Sextus Hive had protection against most conventional weaponry, Oshemar saw need to produce a new, unconventional weapon. Constructing the Unbinding Stone, Oshemar invented a weapon capable of repealing the very laws of physics. Wielding the stone in a final assault on the Hive's queenworld, Oshemar found every boundary in his path, including time itself, destroyed. With the battle won, Oshemar realized too late that the Unbinding Stone could not be stopped, leading to the death of the entire Sextus Hive, then the Caldarans, and everything else in his dominion, with the exception of Oshemar himself, who created a dimensional rift to escape. Unconsciously carrying the stone with him across worlds, he found himself in Asgard, where the stone was somehow rendered inert in the crossing. With his final words, he swore he would find a means to destroy the stone, but died before he could do so.

oshtur.name: Oshtur
oshtur.origin: thumb|left|Oshtur with other Elder Gods ===Origins=== As one of the Elder Gods of Earth, Oshtur was one of the first lifeforms spawned on the planet by its sentient biosphere, the Demiurge, along with Set, Chthon, Gaea, and others. Oshtur had a fascination with the realms beyond Earth, unlike her siblings. ===Early years=== According to legends, after witnessing children play, Oshtur was moved and gave birth to Agamotto. She instructed Agamotto then left him to undertake the paths of magic. Agamotto was in fact sired before Oshtur left Earth. Oshtur left in the days before the Elder Gods were expelled, tens of thousands of years before the conflict among the Elder Gods and their degeneration into malevolent demons. It is unknown for how long Oshtur left Earth, but it is presumed to be millions of years. While exploring the universe, she met a companion in Hoggoth, and they eventually departed the traditional universe for a mystic dimension, where the two resided. Upon Agamotto's passing, Oshtur formed the Vishanti with him and Hoggoth. Oshtur was also responsible for creating the Tome of Oshtur and the Book of the Vishanti. ===Early Ages=== Across the early ages of mankind, Oshtur and the Vishanti, or Eternal Ones ====Great Cataclysm==== During the Great Cataclysm, the cosmic alien entity known as the Other (The Deathblood, one of the Extinction King's lost Extinction Weapons), destroyed Atlantis. The Vishanti shielded the witch Agatha Harkness. In shame, the Vishanti later claimed to be Agatha's saviors and placed an Uroath upon her. ====Age of Acheron and Hyborian Age==== Oshtur created the Bird-Men, a race of winged humanoids, to fight against the bestial races spawned by Set andChthon. For eons they lived in Akah Ma'at city floated high above Cimmeria, enshrouded by clouds. The floating city was dedicated to Oshtur, in her guise as Ma'at, the Goddess of Truth. During the Hyborian Age, after the prophet Epemitreus died circa 11,500 BC, the Eternal Ones set him at Golamira as Man's guardian. During the Age of Conan, circa 10,000 BC, all went according to their wishes from Epemitreus' first meeting with King Conan of Aquilonia, and until the threat of the Red Shadows arose in Hyboria.{{r|Conan the Barbarian Annual Vol 1 7|/ : Conan of the Isles: Part I: Red Shadows and Black Kraken!}} It remains unclear if those Eternal Ones were the Vishanti. ===Modern Age=== ====Kubik and Kosmos==== The Vishanti appeared to the entities Kubik and Kosmos on their tour of the planes of existence, alongside various other deities, abstract concepts and cosmic entities. ====The Cornerstones ==== Ian McNee had a vision of Oshtur in which he is assigned to find the Four Cornerstones of Creation. He later learned that this was a deception by Chthon, and the real Oshtur interceded. ====Strange Academy==== After the Vishanti granted Doctor Strange the request to teach and prepare the magical youth, Strange Academy contracted a high debt to Hoggoth, who hate the magical cost to allow the Strange Academy to exist. After Emily Bright of Strange Academy siphoned the power of two beings (including her classmate Doyle Dormammu) and collapsed, Doctor Strange was unable to unable to help her . He decided to plea for Hoggoth's help despite the already tremendous debt. Despite being angered by Strange's request, Hoggoth removed most of the magics from Emily, though wasn't unable to fully cleanse her. The combination of the chaos caused by the Death of Doctor Strange along with the cost of the Strange Academy eventually led to Hoggoth's collapse. Hoggoth seemingly recuperated afterwards. Later, during Strange Academy's First Year Commencement Ceremony, Emily Bright and Dormammu's army stepped on the Academy's ground to confront both teachers and students. Dormammu and his army were transported by the faculty staff to the Vishanti's plane where Oshtur, Agamotto and Hoggoth attacked them, while Bright and her followers were opposed by Doyle Dormammu and his fellow students. During the battle, as Doyle and Bright unleashed their powers at each other, Bright pierced the dimensional boundaries to tap directly into Hoggoth's magic core, the cue for Dormammu to retreat as the prophecy was accomplishing, starting the "Dawn of Bright". Voodoo asked Hoggoth to transport them back to Strange Academy, where Doyle had taken back his magic from Bright, and awas about to lose control of that power. Witnessing the noble act of Doyle, Hoggoth intervened and swallowed the dark magic from Doyle, saving him. ====Return of General Strange==== To counter the return of General Strange, Doctor Strange consulted the Vishanti who revealed they couldn't track the General, as any search for him led to the Doctor, and informed him that the General would resume the War and use Earth as his war camp and its inhabitants conscripts, but feared he would go after the Vishanti rather than the Trinity of Ashes. Afterwards, the Vishanti confronted Strange for having not destroye

The Vishanti shielded the witch Agatha Harkness. In shame, the Vishanti later claimed to be Agatha's saviors and placed an Uroath upon her. ====Age of Acheron and Hyborian Age==== Oshtur created the Bird-Men, a race of winged humanoids, to fight against the bestial races spawned by Set andChthon. For eons they lived in Akah Ma'at city floated high above Cimmeria, enshrouded by clouds. The floating city was dedicated to Oshtur, in her guise as Ma'at, the Goddess of Truth. During the Hyborian Age, after the prophet Epemitreus died circa 11,500 BC, the Eternal Ones set him at Golamira as Man's guardian. During the Age of Conan, circa 10,000 BC, all went according to their wishes from Epemitreus' first meeting with King Conan of Aquilonia, and until the threat of the Red Shadows arose in Hyboria.{{r|Conan the Barbarian Annual Vol 1 7|/ : Conan of the Isles: Part I: Red Shadows and Black Kraken!}} It remains unclear if those Eternal Ones were the Vishanti. ===Modern Age=== ====Kubik and Kosmos==== The Vishanti appeared to the entities Kubik and Kosmos on their tour of the planes of existence, alongside various other deities, abstract concepts and cosmic entities. ====The Cornerstones ==== Ian McNee had a vision of Oshtur in which he is assigned to find the Four Cornerstones of Creation. He later learned that this was a deception by Chthon, and the real Oshtur interceded. ====Strange Academy==== After the Vishanti granted Doctor Strange the request to teach and prepare the magical youth, Strange Academy contracted a high debt to Hoggoth, who hate the magical cost to allow the Strange Academy to exist. After Emily Bright of Strange Academy siphoned the power of two beings (including her classmate Doyle Dormammu) and collapsed, Doctor Strange was unable to unable to help her . He decided to plea for Hoggoth's help despite the already tremendous debt. Despite being angered by Strange's request, Hoggoth removed most of the magics from Emily, though wasn't unable to fully cleanse her. The combination of the chaos caused by the Death of Doctor Strange along with the cost of the Strange Academy eventually led to Hoggoth's collapse. Hoggoth seemingly recuperated afterwards. Later, during Strange Academy's First Year Commencement Ceremony, Emily Bright and Dormammu's army stepped on the Academy's ground to confront both teachers and students. Dormammu and his army were transported by the faculty staff to the Vishanti's plane where Oshtur, Agamotto and Hoggoth attacked them, while Bright and her followers were opposed by Doyle Dormammu and his fellow students. During the battle, as Doyle and Bright unleashed their powers at each other, Bright pierced the dimensional boundaries to tap directly into Hoggoth's magic core, the cue for Dormammu to retreat as the prophecy was accomplishing, starting the "Dawn of Bright". Voodoo asked Hoggoth to transport them back to Strange Academy, where Doyle had taken back his magic from Bright, and awas about to lose control of that power. Witnessing the noble act of Doyle, Hoggoth intervened and swallowed the dark magic from Doyle, saving him. ====Return of General Strange==== To counter the return of General Strange, Doctor Strange consulted the Vishanti who revealed they couldn't track the General, as any search for him led to the Doctor, and informed him that the General would resume the War and use Earth as his war camp and its inhabitants conscripts, but feared he would go after the Vishanti rather than the Trinity of Ashes. Afterwards, the Vishanti confronted Strange for having not destroye
fields.personality: Oshtur herself was known to be very kind and noble, as demonstrated as her Egyptian alias, Ma'at, who was the Goddess of truth, law, order, and justice. Oshtur appeared to have strong favor for the bloodline of Ororo Munroe. For some unknown reason, since the dawn of Atlantis, this line of African women was given distinguishing features of white hair, blue eyes, and powerful magic potential.
weaknesses: If ever Oshtur was to return to Earth permanently, it is likely the Demogorge would compulsively seek to target her, though her benevolence, magical skill, affiliation with Gaea, and Atum's current demise would limit her chances of harm.
fields.notes: Oshtur's name was possibly inspired by the Cthulhu Mythos being Hastur, or by the Mesopotamian goddess Ishtar.
fields.trivia: Oshtur is associated with the Star card in Tarot, and thus with Jennifer Kale.

osinga rplss.origin: Sapper is a Rajak. When Ultimo wiped out the Rajaks that were on the planet Rajak, Sapper was among the Rajaks that were off-world at the time that chose to hunt Ultimo. He arrived on Earth with Golden-Blade to crash the festivities held on board the USS Constitution. They ran afoul of Ms. Marvel who repelled them. Iron Man later heard of another fight between Ms. Marvel and Sapper and Golden Blade, and arrived to help Ms. Marvel where a miscalculation resulted in Sapper exploding. The S.S. Joseph C. Gillis came under attack by Sapper and Golden Blade. Iron Man managed to defeat them, but Sapper's energy-stealing plot managed to awaken Ultimo. When Ultimo awakened and began to destroy the S.S. Joseph C. Gillis, Sapper and Golden-Blade assisted the crew in evacuating to the lifeboats. Iron Man traced Ultimo's origin to Sapper and learned that Sapper was reviving the Rajaks in mechanoid form. When Ultimo read Sapper's mind, he headed off to attack Sapper's hidden ship as Iron Man discovered that Ultimo's path would go through Spokane. As Ultimo made his way towards Sapper's hidden ship, Iron Man worked with Sapper and Golden-Blade to fight Ultimo. With help from some codes and S.H.I.E.L.D., Iron Man defeated Ultimo as Sapper and Golden-Blade left Earth in their ship.

osiris.name: Osiris
osiris.origin: thumb|right ===Origin and early years=== Osiris was a member of the Heliopolitan race of gods who lived in Heliopolis, Egypt. He was the eldest of Geb, god of earth, and Nut, goddess of the heavens, the brother of Seth, Isis and Nephthys. and was the Egyptian benevolent god of the dead. He married his sister Isis and sired Horus. With Seth's wife Nephthys, he also sired Anubis, causing Seth's resentment. ===Ruler of the Ennead=== As Geb stepped down from rulership, Osiris was chosen to succeed him, to the dismay of Set who wished to rule Heliopolis. During his rule, Osiris placed mortal pharaoh in charge of Heliopolis, allowing the gods to be less involved in mortal affairs and relocate to the their home in the extradimensional realm of Celestial Heliopolis. Some time before 3000 BC, Osiris and his army protected Egypt from an invasion by Chiyou and his demons and were narrowly defeated. ===Hyborian Age=== Osiris was seemingly worshiped in Stygia as Oris or Osiris the Man-Woman. ===1000 BC=== Seeking revenge for impregnating Nephtys, Seth locked Osiris in a coffin and later scattered pieces of his brother throughout Egypt. Osiris' family (Isis, Osiris and Anubis) managed to resurrect him using magic, but after Horus and Osiris were defeated they and Isis were imprisoned in a pyramid for three thousand years by Seth. During that period of imprisonment, Thoth ruled over the Ennead. At some point, Osiris fathered Razan, the Night-Jackal, an half-goddess. Later, For reasons unrevealed, he sentenced her to a 2,000 year imprisonment. ===Modern Age=== thumb|left|Osiris and Thor Odinson (Earth-616)|Thor Osiris , Horus and Isis were finally freed in modern times, where they encountered Thor and Odin. Osiris participated in the Ceremony of Rebirth which reincarnated Odin as Atum-Ra. Osiris aided Thor in defeating Seth. When the former Iron Fist Danny Rand was killed and sent to the Duat, he requested Osiris to return to the mortal realm to protect his successors Pei and Lin Lie from Quan Yaozu. Judging Danny's soul to be noble, Osiris agreed to make Danny his avatar to enact his vengeance upon Quan. Osiris implanted his symbol on Danny's chest, which bestowed him with new powers, and trained him. Months later, Osiris resurrected Danny as the Ghost Fist and tasked him with killing Quan for his soul to judge before a tapestry representing Danny's time on Earth completely burnt out, or else Danny's soul would remain dead. Osiris mentally guided Ghost Fist while he fought his way to the Rand Building to face Quan. Osiris and Orson Randall watched from the Underworld as Ghost Fist and T'an-Long succeeded in enacting their vengeance upon Quan before Danny's tapestry could burn away. When Danny returned to the Duat, Osiris considered their bargain fulfilled and allowed him to rest and go in peace until he would be needed again. Osiris and Danny were visited by Loki, who informed them of Lin Feng's destruction of the Seven Capital Cities of Heaven and the deaths of the Immortal Weapons. Osiris initially refused to let Danny leave to stop Feng until Loki revealed that Feng was the avatar of Chiyou; Osiris then sent Danny to stop Chiyou's resurrection. When Danny sacrificed himself to help Lin Lie deal a powerful blow to Chiyou, he was sent back to the Hall of Truth, where Osiris confirmed him of Lie's victory.

oskar kessler.name: Oskar Kessler
oskar kessler.origin: Captain Kessler was a member of the Nazis who was active during World War II. He was a brilliant inventor who came up with designs for massive robots that could be piloted by soldiers. It was not until March of 1943 that one of his superiors took his plans seriously. This man would be Admiral von Roeder who was then the most recent of many Nazis charged with eliminating the Sub-Mariner by orders directly from Adolf Hitler. Kessler built an army of his robots to invade Atlantis in order to draw out the Sub-Mariner. Namor led his fellow Atlanteans on a counter attack. During the course of the battle, Namor was believed to be dead, and Kessler and von Roeder, believing their operation to be a success then left. Namor survived and followed after them, pushing their robot down an underwater trench. The oceans pressures then caused their robot to rupture, killing both men. Namor sent the severed head of their robot to the shores of Germany as a warning against other Nazis to never attack his home again.

ossawa.name: Ossawa
ossawa.origin: Ossawa was an abnormally large condor that lived during the days of the American Frontier. The massive bird hunted the plains where the Comanche tribe led by Grey Eagle also hunted, threatening the food supply of the tribe. When Red Warrior discovered the bird, he determined that it must die so that his tribe could still hunt for food. Climbing up to the birds next, Reed Warrior had found that Ossawa had laid three eggs and smashed them all. Ossawa then attacked Red Warrior, who fought the condor off with his knife. The massive bird of prey returned for another attack but was struck in the heart by one of Red Warrior's arrows and fell to her death. Red Warrior took one of Ossawa's feathers as a trophy of his victory.

ossem.name: Ossem
ossem.origin: Ossem was one of the great patriarchs of the Atlanteans 2000 years ago. Most of Ossem's sons were slaughtered by Atlantean barbarians. Ossem's son Balaal began recruiting followers for the ancient god Set and denounced the Atlantean's god Neptune demanding revenge against the barbarians who killed his brothers while Ossem preached pacifism. When Ossem asked Neptune to intercede, he was originally rebuffed and was told that Neptune did not perform parlor tricks for the weak of faith. Ossem was later captured by Balaal's cult of Set followers who had created a proto-Serpent Crown called the Golden Serpent powered by their psychic energy in the hopes of returning Set to Earth. When the cult tried to sacrifice Ossem, Neptune rained down destruction killing everyone in the cult, but spared Ossem. The Atlantean people at this point scattered and Ossem spent the rest of his life reuniting his people. On his deathbed, Neptune promised Ossem from that point forward he would take a more active role in protecting the Atlanteans. The period where Neptune nurtured the Atlanteans people and dwelt amongst them is seen as a golden age in Atlantean history.

oswald brotherhood.origin: Oswald was a young member of the Brotherhood, assigned by Hoffman to blow up a disco in his native Moscow. This task done, he eventually travelled to the United States of America he saved Fagin and Asher from an antimutant mob by blowing them up, as well.

oswald boeglin.name: Oswald Boeglin
oswald boeglin.origin: Not much was known of the mutant known as Bulwark before he was found and recruited by Emplate. This powerhouse joined a team that Emplate gathered to torment Generation X, including Murmur, Vincente, and DOA. Before the young teens returned to the Massachusetts Academy from their outing into the city, they were attacked by Emplate's Hellions. Skin, who had separated from the group to drop off Synch at his parents' house was ambushed by Bulwark and brought back to the Institute. The Hellions were successful in capturing the young mutants, but M had telepathically called for help and it was answered by the X-Man Bishop. M took out her frustrations on Bulwark, punching him through the school's Bio-Sphere and then flying after him. As he was about to attack M, his muscles suddenly withered away. Knowing that he was defeated, he fled along with Vincente. Leech—then a ward of Generation X and resident of the Bio-dome—was the one responsible for the atrophy of Bulwark's powers, and M thanked him for his help. With Penance's realignment of alliances Generation X was successful in stopping the team. Bulwark did not have a happy ending. Sometime later he was captured by operatives of the revamped Weapon X program. Along with many other mutants, he was rounded up and put into a concentration camp called Neverland and was subsequently killed in the gas chambers.

oswald silkworth.name: Oswald Silkworth
oswald silkworth.origin: The Arranger was the right-hand man to Wilson Fisk, a.k.a. the Kingpin. Oswald was deemed the Arranger because of his 'arranging' of Fisk's day-to-day business dealings, be they legal or otherwise. This gave the Kingpin more time to deal with personal matters such as his wife's illness, or his personal vendetta against Daredevil. The Arranger was very good at his job, able to plan ahead almost as well as his employer, and provide contingency plans in case of failure. He'd most often come into conflict with Spider-Man, although the web-slinger ultimately saved his life from the Punisher. His status as Fisk's number one trustee began to falter when he botched an assassination attempt on the Lobo brothers, allowing them to retaliate in a brutal gang war. Again, Oswald counted on Spider-Man to save his life, but the Kingpin was now aware that the Arranger was losing control. After the loss of a huge chunk of territory to Hammerhead and the Chameleon, Oswald's multiple failings finally put him on Kingpin's termination list, and a hit was put out on his life. In his final hours, he placed a call to Spider-Man for help, but Spidey figured it was yet another trap and refused. He was murdered by British assassins Knight and Fogg later that night. Spider-Man did seek justice against the duo later, feeling bad that he didn't accept Oswald's cry for help.

other alien entity.name: Other (Alien Entity)
other alien entity.species: Cosmic Being; Alien; Extinction Weapon ("cursed idea woven with Mortoturgy")
other alien entity.origin: The being known only as the Other is an extra-dimensional being that manifests in our reality as a race of diminutive grey-skinned humanoids. Although they appear as an entire species, they are in fact just projections of the same mind and have no real existence independent of it. For countless millennia, it has been engaged in a war with the cosmic being known as the Scrier for control of the multiverse. According to the Vishanti, the Other is in truth one of the Extinction King's lost Extinction Weapons called Deathblood, a war-machine of their own making, because it was forged in their ancient struggle against it, and the force responsible for the Great Cataclysm that sank Atlantis. In shame, the Vishanti later claimed to be Agatha Harkness' saviors, when in reality they were merely attempting to clean up a catastrophe born of their own long-standing failure. In 1947, the Other visited the planet Zenn-La, and destroyed every living being and structure on the planet, killing Shalla-Bal alongside countless others. Their presence was enough to render Galactus and the Silver Surfer comatose and unable to interfere. Several years later, the Other would abduct several humans from Earth, including comics writer Stan Lee and widow Henrietta Rose. Finding Lee unsuitable for their purposes, they soon returned him to his office with his memory erased, but subjected Rose to various painful experiments. She would be rescued by the Silver Surfer, despite the Other's attempts to destroy him. In the modern age, the Other would once again return to Earth, tormenting Henrietta Rose and her daughter. The Silver Surfer once again confronted it, driving its influence from Rose's mind, but was overwhelmed by swarms of the Other's creatures when he attempted to pursue it back to its own dimension. The Other infected him, attempting to erase him from the memories of every being in existence. In attempting to cure him, Agatha Harkness briefly made mental contact with the Other and was almost destroyed herself. Eventually, working alongside Scrier, the Silver Surfer was able to barricade shut the portal between dimensions, trapping the Other within. When Asgard was displaced to Earth, this disrupted the barricade sufficiently that the Other was once again able to manifest beyond its own dimension. Scrier attempted to manipulate Thor into sacrificing himself to placate the Other, but the agreement was interrupted by Galactus, who threatened to attack both players in this ancient conflict. Fearing the destruction that would ensure from such a conflict, the Other agreed to a half-billion year truce with Scrier.

other spider totem.name: Other (Spider-Totem)
other spider totem.origin: ===Origin=== The Spider-Man of Earth-616 was chosen by the Great Weaver to be the receptacle of the Other when he became Spider-Man. However, Spider-Man subconsciously rejected and suppressed the spider side of himself until he encountered the Inheritor Morlun, who fed on the essence of totemic avatars. After vanquishing Morlun and becoming aware of his totemic abilities for the first time, Peter Parker began to weaken - discovering he was dying of an unknown mystical affliction - and concurrently had prophetic visions of his death at the hands of the Morlun, who had returned from death. When Morlun finally made his move and mortally wounded Peter, the Other took over Peter's body and killed the Inheritor. After Peter seemingly died from his injuries, the Other transported his body to the Brooklyn Bridge and spun a cocoon. The Other confronted Peter's psyche within his mindscape, claiming to be the manifestation of his totemic spider-powers and telling him that his human side had died, but that he could return to life if he embraced his spider side. Peter reluctantly agreed, and emerged from the cocoon completely healed of his prior wounds and with enhanced powers - thereby "conquering" death. 150px|left|thumb|As the Great Weaver (Multiverse)|Great Weaver Shortly after Peter's resurrection, the Other manifested as a swarm of pirate spiders and attacked Stark Tower to eat Peter's old shed skin, cocooning the top of Stark Tower in webbing. When he arrived, Spider-Man discovered that the spiders had used his shed skin to form a humanoid body similar to the Gatekeeper, albeit being distinctly female in shape. Spider-Man attempted to fight her using his augmented powers, but the Other's manifestation retreated, easily ripping through a vibranium-reinforced wall. Declaring herself to be Spider-Man's "Other," the entity explained to Peter that Morlun should have killed him, but the Great Weaver had resurrected him. The female entity stated that another spider-totem had opposed this and sent her to kill Peter and restore the natural order. Calling herself "Ero" after the genus of spider comprising her body, the female creature claimed she was Peter's opposite, his nemesis and his significant other; warning him to "evolve or die" before escaping down a drain. 150px|right|thumb|As Ero Ero retreated to an old church across the street from Stark Tower, where she spun a cocoon and took on a human form that was the opposite of Peter in every way: female to his male, dark-skinned to his light, and blonde to his brown hair. Sometime later, Spider-Man met up with Beast at the old church, where they discovered Ero's empty cocoon. ===Civil War=== Having taken on human form, Ero assumed the name "Miss Arrow" and became the school nurse at Midtown High School to monitor and test Peter. When Midtown High was attacked by three Mysterios, Miss Arrow found herself in contact with Quentin Beck. Beck implied that she was more than an innocent bystander, mentioning that he knew about Miss Arrow's "superiors," and that he could easily see through her charade. He told her that she must work to keep Peter at the school because his superiors wanted it, and so did hers; though Arrow claimed to not know what he was talking about. Beck vanished, although Arrow later found herself face-to-face with Francis Klum. Klum attempted to take her hostage, telling that she was to become a pawn in a much larger game. Angered, Arrow revealed her true nature to him by extending large stingers from her wrists. Telling Klum she was no one's pawn, she plunged one of them into his chest. Before she could finish him off, he teleported. 150px|left|thumb|As Miss Arrow Arrow later convinced Spider-Man to stay at the school, a task which was complicated when Peter became a fugitive for going against the Registration Act, as he had to use an Image Inducer to disguise himself as "Ben Reilly" to continue his career at the school. When Debra Whitman got into an altercation with Flash Thompson, Arrow moved to attack her with her stingers but was distracted when Betty Brant remarked that she and Flash used to date. Despite being tempted to attack Betty as well, Arrow shook her hand instead, making the veiled threat to eat her. Flash and Betty Brant went on a date, which clashed with Arrow's plans for Flash. When Betty had to use the restroom, Ero emerged from the toilet as thousands of spiders, frightening Betty. When Flash and the restaurant manager came to the scene after Betty had left the bathroom, only some cocaine and straw were found, making the manager think Betty had used the cocaine. Later at Midtown High, Peter Parker was talking to Flash when Arrow walked into the room. Peter barely activated the image inducer in time to conceal his true face from her. Peter found it strange that his spider-sense hadn't warned him of Arrow's approach, since in the past it had always warned him when there was a risk of somebody seeing him and learning his secret identity. When Flash and the restaurant manager came to the scene after Betty had left the bathroom, only some cocaine and straw were found, making the manager think Betty had used the cocaine. Later at Midtown High, Peter Parker was talking to Flash when Arrow walked into the room. Peter barely activated the image inducer in time to conceal his true face from her. Peter found it strange that his spider-sense hadn't warned him of Arrow's approach, since in the past it had always warned him when there was a risk of somebody seeing him and learning his secret identity. abilities: When manifested as Ero/Miss Arrow, it could into a swarm of spiders and control them. It also acquired sufficient medical knowledge to act as a nurse.
fields.notes: portrays Miss Arrow in . Due to the events of Mephisto rewriting history, the powers Peter developed during The Other (and the powers obtained from his incident with the Queen) have mysteriously disappeared. The manifestation of the entity known as Miss Arrow would never exist outside of The Other story arc, though the Other appeared in its "Ero" and giant spider forms in the Scarlet Spider series. Ero was introduced as an antagonistic spider totem opposed to the Great Weaver, who had resurrected Peter Parker, and manifested to kill him and restore the natural order. However, a retcon implemented during combined Ero with aspects of the Great Weaver into "The Other", an entity whose nature has been expanded upon in Spider-Verse. The remaining aspects of the Great Weaver, such as weaving the Web of Life, were given to the Master Weaver. According to Uatu, the Other is the manifestation of Peter's spider abilities and a representative of the Great Weaver. This was retconned in and Spider-Verse, which established the Other as an entity independent of Spider-Man - who possesses powers regardless of whether he is its vessel or not. According to Old Man Spider, The Other, The Bride and The Scion are unique totemic entities in the Multiverse. The retcon that the Other was the spider-totem who resurrected Peter leaves its reasons for manifesting as Ero and trying to kill Peter unclear. According to the , the Other is unique to Earth-616, though this is proven false by it resurrecting the Peter Parker of Earth-982 and has attempted to claim the Peter Parker of Earth-70134 as its avatar.
fields.trivia: Ero is similar in appearance to the Gatekeeper, and at one point appears as the Gatekeeper, though whether they were meant to be related or one-in-the-same is unknown. Its appearance in was based on Spider-Man's costume. The Other has been described as the personification of Spider-Man's spider-powers - and by extension those of his clone Kaine; but despite this it has been rejected by and separated from them and even killed without the total loss of their spider-powers. Despite having repeatedly faced life-threatening danger and often been enraged, the Spider-Man of Earth-616 never transformed into a spider-humanoid monster. During his fight with Spider-Man, Ero stated that the wrist stingers could only be used against threats of supernatural origin. This proved to be false, as Kaine was able to use them whenever they wanted. Although he had been transformed into the Other's form, the Peter Parker of Earth-982 appeared to have been able to retain his human mindset even during the transformation.

otis johnson ii.name: Otis Johnson II
otis johnson ii.species: Human, Mutate Due to a mishap at an A.I.M. facility, Otis was exposed to a chemical blast making him indestructible and impervious to pain
otis johnson ii.origin: ===Early Life=== Otis Danger Johnson was accidentally exposed to a chemical at an A.I.M. facility, making him indestructible and impervious to pain. ===Nightwing Restorations=== Johnson worked as an administrative assistant for the Nightwing Restorations Ltd. and due to the working style of this company he normally helped Colleen Wing and Misty Knight on many cases. He tried to act a tough thug which was very unconvincing. He was attacked by the Atlantean, Orka, who was looking for Misty and Colleen. Being away from the sea caused oxygen imbalance in his brain. Because he could not answer his questions he pummeled Otis around the office. He could not understand why he wouldn't die. After a while stopped hitting Otis and waited patiently for them to return. After that the two became friends. During an investigation of Celia Ricadonna, after the murders of some of their clients, he posed as a parking attendant at an auction she was having to sell a microchip that could destroy the global economy. He later stalled the bodyguards long enough to stop Ricadonna from escaping.. ===Heroes for Hire=== During the Civil War, Misty and Coleen were contacted by Iron Man to reform Heroes for Hire in order to track down superhumans refusing to comply with the Superhuman Registration Act. Initially hesitant, the pair eventually created a team including Shang-Chi, Humbug, Orka, Black Cat, Paladin, and a new Tarantula. Otis was kept on for administration. When Ricadonna planned a prison break, she sent a bomb to their office, destroying it with only Otis inside. Though he was fine, he was concerned about losing his job. Otis went undercover as the pizza delivery guy, but all he was delivering was a box full of smoke screen, allowing to take down a group of criminals. The information they got led them to the Grim Reaper. Otis teamed up with Orka and Shang-Chi to save Humbug from the Headmen. , but sadly his friend was killed. When the team traveled to the Savage Land, Otis stayed behind. However on their return the Hulk was raging war against the city, which lead to the end of the team and leaving him without a job.

otmu.name: Otmu
otmu.origin: Otmu the heretic was responsible for the deaths of a billion of his fellow Watchers by putting forth The Doctrine of Ultimate Non-Interference; wherein that the Watchers can change the outcomes of their observations by merely observing them and that to adhere to their strict rule of non-involvement the Watchers would have to cease to exist in order to not affect anything. Watchers became obsessed with this idea and chose to will themselves to death. When confonted by Quasar and the Stranger Otmu chose to will himself to death. Quasar eventually presented "the Life Affirming Idea" that the Watchers affect the universe even in death and that all things being equal their being alive was the lesser of the two violations of their oath and that alive they can carry out their work.
